questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: Use it regularly to activate the trailer brakes in all driving conditions.
Use it only to test the trailer brakes.
Use it only in bad weather when the trailer may skid.
Use it only when the trailer is carrying a load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use it only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve is for testing the trailer brakes only. Do not use it while driving because it can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: What should you know about driving a bobtail tractor?

options.text: Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail is a tractor with no trailer attached. Bobtails need a longer distance to stop than a tractor pulling a loaded trailer.

questions.question: Which vehicle is most likely to have the "crack-the-whip" effect?

options.text: A five-axle tractor with one trailer
A three-axle tractor with one trailer

questions.explanation: Triple trailers are most likely to have the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: What should you do after finishing a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Leave the rear shut-off valves open.
Leave the emergency line valve open.

questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear shut-off valves to check for air leaks. Then close both shut-off valves before you start driving.

questions.question: What color are emergency air lines usually coded?
questions.explanation: Service air lines are coded blue. Emergency air lines are coded red.

questions.question: When does the automatic tractor protection valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi.
When wheels regain traction after a skid.
When air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. This closes the valve and stops air flow.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When drivers do not drive fast enough.
When drivers pay attention to the road.

questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers take turns at too high a speed. Always turn slowly and safely.

questions.question: Low-clearance trailers are difficult to drive over:
questions.explanation: Low-clearance trailers are hard to drive over railroad crossings. Single-axle tractors pulling long trailers have extra difficulty crossing raised railroad-highway crossings.

questions.question: How do you test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Remove the parking brake control knob.
Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
Release air by pressing the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, let the air supply charge fully, turn off the engine, then press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to emergency position when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: What happens when combination vehicles are lightly loaded?

options.text: Most weight should be in the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Lightly loaded vehicles have poor traction and weaker braking power. The wheels lock up easily when braking.

questions.question: What should the trailer hand valve be used for?

options.text: Working together with the brake pedal.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid. Do not use it for parking because it may release air pressure and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: If your trailer drifts off course while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the top of the steering wheel toward the drift.
Turn the top of the steering wheel away from the drift.
Return the steering wheel to straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel toward the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, correct it immediately by turning the top of the steering wheel toward the direction of the drift.

questions.question: If oil and water build up in the air tanks, what happens to the brakes?

options.text: They may feel soft or mushy.

questions.explanation: Drain air tanks daily to remove water and oil. Too much oil and water in the air tanks can damage how the brakes work.

questions.question: When do large combination vehicles take the longest to stop?
questions.explanation: Empty vehicles take longer to stop than loaded vehicles. With less weight, the wheels have less grip on the road.

questions.question: What can happen if you change lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle?

options.text: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
Other drivers will be confused about your lane choice.

questions.correctAnswerText: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
questions.explanation: Changing lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle can create a "crack-the-whip" effect. This can cause the trailer to roll over.

questions.question: When should the trailer hand valve be used?

options.text: To speed up on rural roads.
Only to test the trailer brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: When inspecting a coupling under the trailer, what should you check?

options.text: Detach the jaws from the kingpin.
Check that the locking lever is in the "emergency" position.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: Look into the back of the fifth wheel to check the coupling. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?
questions.explanation: A combination vehicle has two air lines: the service line and the emergency line.

questions.question: Before backing your tractor under the trailer, the trailer brakes should be:
questions.explanation: Before backing under the trailer, lock the trailer brakes. This is an important safety step when coupling a trailer to a tractor.

questions.question: What is the trailer hand valve used for?

options.text: Checking the connection between trailer and tractor.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes.
